reconstructed_theorem_text:
This packet supplies a function definition, rather than a theorem proposition. For any real normed vector space E, natural m, arbitrary g:E->E, eta,epsilon,h in R, arrays t,b,d:Fin(m)->R and omega:Fin(m) x Fin(m)->R, fuel:E->N, and input w=((X,P),((zeta0,zeta1),(G0,G1))), the defined function returns an element of Option((E x E) x N). The input vectors belong to E and G0,G1:Fin(m)->E; b,d denote positionWeight,momentumWeight.
Set a=exp(-h/2), sigma=sqrt(1-exp(-h)), P0=a P+sigma zeta0 and Y0_i=X+t_i P0. In increasing Fin(m) order, collect calls run(g,eta,epsilon,Y0_i,fuel(Y0_i),Y0_i), mapping each success (x0_i,k0_i) to (Z0_i,k0_i+1) with Z0_i=g(x0_i+sqrt(eta)G0_i). Any failure propagates none. A successful collection returns the array Z0 and Q0=sum_i(k0_i+1). Set Y1_i=Y0_i-sum_j omega_ij Z0_j. Similarly collect run(g,eta,epsilon,Y1_i,fuel(Y1_i),Y1_i), mapping each success (x1_i,k1_i) to (Z1_i,k1_i+1) with Z1_i=g(x1_i+sqrt(eta)G1_i). Failure propagates none. A successful second collection returns Z1 and Q1=sum_i(k1_i+1). Return
  some((X+h P0-sum_j b_j Z1_j,
        a(P0-sum_j d_j Z1_j)+sigma zeta1),Q0+Q1).
The finite exact-real interpreter returns none at zero fuel. At positive fuel it evaluates g(x), sets next=y-eta g(x), and returns (x,1) when ||next-x||<=(1-eta)epsilon. Otherwise it recurses from next with one less fuel and adds one to a successful returned count. collectQueries on zero nodes returns an empty array and count zero; on m+1 nodes it executes the first call, then the recursively collected tail, adding counts and propagating failure.
All sums use all m actual nodes. On success the returned count equals 2m+sum_i(k0_i+k1_i), counting all interpreter evaluations including terminal tests and one additional shifted-point g evaluation per node in each stage. This is an exact-real operational definition with arbitrary supplied vectors, without positivity, regularity, probability-law, sufficient-fuel, measurability, complexity-bound or successful-termination assumptions or conclusions. For m=0 both collections succeed empty with total count zero.

Input type is (E x E) x ((E x E) x ((Fin(m)->E) x (Fin(m)->E))). Return type is Option((E x E) x N). No inner-product, completeness, finite-dimensionality, measurable or probability structure is required.
quantifiers: A definition parameterized by every admissible E,m,g,eta,epsilon,h,t,omega,b,d,fuel,w. It assigns an optional result, rather than proving a proposition or existential successful execution. All m first-stage calls are collected before constructing second-stage calls. The anchor and starting point of each run equal the respective Y-stage value.
assumptions: Only typing and the real normed-space structures. g,fuel,all real parameters and arrays are unrestricted. The input vectors have no distribution assumption; Fin(m) arrays have no source-specific quadrature interpretation. The exact run and collector semantics are as supplied. No parameter positivity, contraction, regularity, measurability or sufficient fuel is assumed.
conclusion: The operational definition returns none on any collected failure. On successful completion it returns the displayed two-stage state update and the sum of stage counts. Its successful count is exactly 2m plus all interpreter evaluation counts, including their terminal successful tests. It does not independently prove success, a count upper bound, output accuracy or a mathematical convergence property.

Failed execution returns none rather than a partial count. Fin(m) denotes exactly m actual nodes. The no-node case returns the empty-sum update and zero count.
